title: Can we make a table of one fourth rotis too?
description: A roti is cut into four equal pieces and the pieces are collected one at a time, the way half rotis were. Each row adds one more piece, and four pieces are checked against a full roti.
teaching_notes: One idea: a table of any fractional unit is made by adding one more of that unit in each row. Watch for students who keep one half as the unit while changing the count.

source: Can you create a similar table for 1/4?
video_script.why: The child builds the table of one fourth the way the table of half rotis was built, adding one more fourth in each row.
video_script.substitution: Swap the half roti for a piece that is one fourth of a roti, and add one more piece in each row.
video_script.anchor: A roti cut into four equal pieces, next to the table of half rotis, with an empty table below
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the table for one fourth is made the same way

final_answer.spoken: yes; one fourth is one times fourth, and two, three and four fourths added are two, three and four times fourth, and four fourths make a full roti

video_script.fraction_reading: one fourth, two fourths, three fourths, four fourths
never_show: any row of the table with its count before the answer beat
maths_rules: a roti cut into 4 equal pieces: each piece is 1/4
written as counts: 1 x 1/4, 2 x 1/4, 3 x 1/4, 4 x 1/4
check: 4 pieces put together make 1 full roti, so 4 x 1/4 = 4/4 = 1
video_script.design: One idea: any fractional unit gives a table by adding one more of it in each row. Same method as the half roti table. The roti pieces and the table stay on the board to the end.
